name: Envelope follower: audio loudness as a modulation source (fold, ring mod, ducking, playback rate)
goal: Use an envelope follower to turn one signal's amplitude into a modulation lane for organic, performance-linked movement instead of a fixed LFO: map it (with depth, rise/fall smoothing, and invert) to wavefolder amount, opposing left/right ring-mod depths, a pad's volume or filter for kick-keyed ducking or expansion, or a looped sample's playback rate.

source.title: Using Envelope Followers for Modulation in Your Music! The How, the When, the Why

prerequisites: Envelope follower that outputs a control signal (CC or internal mod) with depth, rise/attack, fall/release and invert; destination params that can be modulated (fold, ring-mod, filter, channel volume, sample rate)

inputs.name: follower_source
inputs.description: Signal whose loudness drives modulation (the synth itself, a kick, a looped texture)

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Invert so louder source gives lower destination value

outputs.name: follower_mod_route
outputs.description: Audio-driven modulation mapping with tuned depth and smoothing

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Portable alias: envelope follower = amplitude detector → smoothed control signal (Web Audio: AnalyserNode RMS → AudioParam setTargetAtTime).

Delta vs sidechain-compressor-duck-synth-pads and modulation-lfo-envelope-mod-matrix-routing: modulation comes from another signal's loudness, routable to any parameter, not a compressor or a free-running LFO.

steps.action: Contrast with an LFO: an LFO cycles a parameter regardless of the music; an envelope follower raises the parameter when the source gets louder and lowers it when quieter.
steps.expect: Clear choice of follower vs LFO

steps.action: Insert the follower on the source channel, set it to output its envelope as a control signal, and map it to the destination (e.g. wavefolder fold amount) via learn/assign; disable any competing LFO on that parameter.
steps.expect: Destination knob moves with the source's loudness

steps.action: Tune Depth for how aggressive the effect is, and raise Rise/Fall times to reduce volatility (slower up and down movement); lower them for jittery, transient-tracking motion.
steps.expect: Movement matches musical intent, not zipper noise

steps.action: Stereo opposing motion: use the left and right follower outputs on two separate lanes into two ring-mod (or similar) depths, invert one, so one rises as the other falls when the source gets louder.
steps.expect: Two effect params move in opposite directions; L/R difference adds width

steps.action: Kick-keyed motion: follow the kick and map to a pad's channel volume. Non-inverted = sidechain expansion (pad louder on kicks); inverted = ducking (quieter on kicks). Same mapping inverted onto fold or a filter opens the effect in the gaps between kicks.
steps.expect: Pad pumps or opens rhythmically with the kick

steps.action: Texture rate: follow a looped percussive/mechanical sample and map to its own playback rate (faster when loud, slower when quiet); invert to speed up in the gaps. Optionally use that loop's follower to duck a synth.
Optional follower types where available: pitch follower (higher pitch → higher value) and spectral-brightness follower (brighter → higher value) instead of amplitude.

verification: Destination value rises with source loudness (or falls when inverted)
Increasing rise/fall visibly smooths the control curve
Kick-keyed volume mapping produces audible ducking when inverted and expansion when not
